[h1] An interesting game, held back by its extreme difficulty. [/h1]

[i] This would be a "Neutral" review if that were an option. Recommended for tower defense enthusiasts, not recommended for completionists. [/i]

Most of Dungeon Warfare is engaging and rewarding, but some design decisions left me baffled. The endgame leveling curve is painfully slow considering how little reward it offers, and certain stages (especially The Mountain) feel disproportionately harder than the rest of the game.

This absolutely should not be a game that demands 100+ hours to complete. Of my 122 total hours played, around 30 were spent grinding Endless mode on various stages just to gain XP, along with dozens of failed attempts to clear The Mountain with 8 runes enabled.

That left a bitter taste at the very end of what was otherwise a good experience. Because of these absurd design choices, I won’t be trying Dungeon Warfare 2 or 3.

[h1]ストーリー[/h1] 
あなたはダンジョンの主（ダンジョン・ロード） 
薄暗い地下の領地に、今日もまた「勇者」だの「冒険者」だのと名乗る泥棒どもが、あなたの財宝目当てに押し寄せてくる。彼らをもてなすのは、壁から飛び出す槍、床から突き上げるスパイク、そして奈落へと突き落とすプッシュトラップ。 
さあ、慈悲なき防衛戦の始まりだ。彼らの死体でダンジョンの床を舗装しよう。

[h1]概要[/h1] 
かつての「Armor Games」や「Kongregate」といったFlashゲーム黄金期を彷彿とさせる、ドット絵スタイルのタワーディフェンス（TD）

敵の進行ルート上に罠を設置して撃退するという基本ルールに加え、物理演算を利用した「地形活用」が最大の特徴。 ただダメージを与えるだけでなく、重い鉄球で敵を吹き飛ばして奈落（穴）に落としたり、トロッコで轢き殺したりと、サディスティックな罠コンボを決めることができる。

[h1]感想[/h1] 
[b]「理不尽」こそが最高のスパイス。マゾヒストな戦略家たちへ贈る、死に覚えゲーの佳作。[/b]

このゲームをプレイすると、強烈なデジャヴに襲われる。 
それは、かつてブラウザゲームに熱中したあの頃の、「シンプルだが奥深く、そして死ぬほど難しい」あの感覚だ。 グラフィックは粗いドット絵だが、大量の敵兵が罠にかかり、物理演算でラグドールのようにお手玉され、悲鳴を上げて穴に落ちていく様は、現代のAAA級ゲームにも勝るカタルシスがある。

しかし、本作の真骨頂はその「難易度」にある。 
中盤以降は、ただ罠を置くだけでは絶対にクリアできない。「ここで敵を止めて、あそこでまとめて吹き飛ばす」というミリ単位の調整と、完璧な解法（キルゾーンの構築）が求められる。その過程はまさに「理不尽」の一言。一瞬の判断ミスで防衛線が崩壊し、大量の敵になだれ込まれる絶望感。

だが、その理不尽さを乗り越え、完璧な防衛ラインを構築した時の脳汁が出るような達成感は、TD好きにはたまらないご褒美だ。

[h1]評価[/h1] 
【GOOD】 
・敵を物理的に「吹き飛ばして」穴に落とす快感。他のTDにはない、物理演算を駆使したトラップ連携が最高に楽しい。 
・「ルーン」システムにより、敵を強化して経験値を稼ぐか、難易度を下げるかといったリスク管理ができるやり込み要素。 
・古き良きFlashゲームの遺伝子を受け継いだ、シンプルながらも中毒性の高いゲームプレイ。

【BAD】 
・[b]「解法」の狭さ。[/b] 難易度が上がると「自由なトラップ配置で守る」というよりは、「開発者が想定した唯一の正解（パズル）を見つける」作業になりがちで、戦略の自由度が極端に狭まるステージがある。 
・経験値（XP）によるトラップのレベル上げが必須であり、詰まったら過去のステージを何度も周回してレベルを上げる「グラインド（作業）」を強要される。 
・ドット絵が細かすぎて、大量の敵が重なると何が起きているのか視認しづらく、いつの間にか突破されていることがある。
So good and it has sequels, one of the best tower defenses in 2D.

Got this on sale for around $2 and it's probably one of the best value for the money games I've ever bought. I enjoy tower defense but I almost wish trap defense was it's own genre. This game fills the seemingly rare niche of using traps instead of pure towers. Most tower defense games have some building off to the side shooting an occasional arrow at passing enemies but this game, like orcs must die in away, has them standing in front of flamethrowers, being pushed off cliffs, and ground to pieces.

The game has pretty basic graphics but it works in its favor in its own way. The low graphic requirement means any computer can probably play this as the multiple hundreds of enemies are trying to rush to the core. The game also has a mild villain protagonist theme. The levels are pretty varied and a lot have quite a few ways to win them. 

The game does have some downsides but these will vary depending on what kind of gamer you are. There are a lot of levels to play, by the middle of them I was really digging into how I could come back to beat the level without losing any lives or with some runes on, but by the end of the last level I'd just had my fill and didn't have any desire left to replay any levels. The first missions feel really limited because you don't have many traps, but at later levels you'll probably have a handful of traps you always bring so the game starts to feel a bit same-y. The game has a pretty hardcore subset of fans that will try and set records on the infinite mode or beat every mission with 10 of the runes (optional modifiers that give an exp multiplier but come with a downside like making enemies stronger/faster/heavier or limiting traps, lives, etc) but without self imposed challenges it was one and done for me, still there's plenty here.

The levels vary greatly in difficulty, towards mid game you'll start getting people that rush fast enough to set off some traps without being hit, later still you'll get horse riding enemies that will absolutely blaze through your setup if you're not expecting them. Some maps don't let you set up a single killbox by joining the paths, others will have what basically amount troll setups, like having a pit that seems like it'd be great to use but then turns out the level is entirely made of people that will outrun any push or spring trap. The bonus casino stage has special units that are so high in hp they're basically pointless to try and kill with damage and you're best left tossing them off the cliffs. A few levels had flying enemies that are immune to most traps and pretty unfun to play against.

If you're a fan of trap based game this one is definitely worth the price.

▷평점 : ★★★☆☆
Dungeon Warfare

2015년도에 출시한, 타워디펜스류 인디게임.
호불호가 굉장히 강하게 갈릴 수 있는 난이도를 자랑한다.

필자는 '타워디펜스'를 매우 좋아한다.
하지만 감히 이 게임에 대해서 말하자면, '마음 편히 무지성'으로 할 수 있는 게임이 아니라고 생각한다.
BloonsTD, 워크래프트3 유즈맵, 스타크래프트1,2 유즈맵을 생각했다면, 스트레스받을 수 있는 난이도라고 말하고 싶다.


▶게임 요소
1개의 스테이지마다 최대 3개의 별을 달성할 수 있다.
타워디펜스 특성상, 놓친 몬스터 수에 따라 획득 별이 감소된다.

[스테이지 클리어]
각 스테이지를 클리어하면, 배치할 수 있는 신규 타워를 획득하거나, 신규 액티브 스킬, 신규 룬조각(?), 보석을 획득할 수 있다.
- 신규 타워 : 각 스테이지마다 배치할 수 있는 타워.
- 액티브 스킬 : 여러 종류의 효과를 유저 입맛에 따라 배치 및 사용할 수 있는 요소.
- 룬조각(?) : 각 스테이지마다 제약을 걸어서 획득할 수 있는 경험치를 증가시키는 요소
- 보석 : 타워, 액티브, 패시브 스킬의 레벨을 올릴 수 있는 요소.

[플레이어 레벨]
스테이지를 클리어하면, XP를 획득할 수 있다.
여러 종류의 룬조각(?)을 선택하여 게임 내 제약을 걸어 획득XP를 더 상승시킬 수 있다.
획득 XP로 플레이어 레벨이 상승하며, 게임 내에 배치할 수 있는 타워 상한선이 증가하며 타워 레벨을 올릴 수 있는 보석을 획득할 수 있다.

[타워 업그레이드]
여타 타워디펜스 게임처럼, 타워를 업그레이드시키면 다른 테크트리로 갈아탈 수 있다.
단, A타워를 3개 설치해도 딱 1개만 상위 테크트리로 업그레이드시킬 수 있다는 제한된(?) 요소가 있다.


▶난이도
이 게임의 난이도는 앞서 말한 바와 같이, 어려운 편이다.
무지성으로는 절대 3별을 달성할 수 없다.
그러므로, 매 스테이지마다 두뇌 풀가동(?)을 해야지만 별3개를 달성할 만큼 초반부터 어려운 난이도를 가지고 있다.
그리고 후반부로 갈수록 점점 변태(?)같은 난이도로 별 1개도 클리어하기 어려운 수준으로 밸런스가 잡혀있다.

개인적으로 퍼즐류&아케이드류는 적정 난이도로 설계되는 것이 가장 좋다고 생각한다.
무슨 뜻이냐면, 개발자가 의도로 설계했지만 유저는 마치 '내가 똑똑해서 쉽게 클리어했다' 라고 느끼게 하는 것을 뜻한다.
그러므로 유저 수준이 1~100까지 있다고 가정하면, 약 35~40 수준으로 설계되는 것이 가장 베스트가 아닐까 한다.

왜 이런 말을 쓰고 있냐면,
필자에게 이 게임이 어느 순간 스트레스 요소로 다가왔기 때문이다.
후반부로 갈수록 너무 '악의적인' 느낌의 밸런스로 설계되었기 때문에, "이걸 개발자도 깰 수 있는건가?" 라는 의문이 드는 스테이지가 몇몇 있었다.
원래 게임은 유저마다 '주관적인' 플레이로 자유롭게 즐길 수 있도록 해줘야 한다.
하지만, 이 게임은 중후반부 스테이지부터 '객관적인' 설계로 모범 답안지가 존재하는 것처럼 밸런싱이 되어있다.
이럴 거면, "각 타워에 레벨 요소가 왜 있는 것일까?", "왜 자유롭게 타워를 배치할 수 있게 되어있는 것일까?" 라는 의문도 들었다.

「게임은 어려워야 재미있다」라고 말하는 사람이 있다.
하지만, 돌파구가 제시되어있어야 어려워도 재미를 느끼는거지, 돌파구도 제시되어있지 않은데 난이도만 어렵게 설정했다면, 이건 밸런스적 문제라고 본다.
뭐랄까... RPG로 따지면, 난이도가 어려운 지역이 개방되었는데 그 지역에 입장하기 위해서 강해지기 위한 컨텐츠가 없는 느낌이랄까..?

타워디펜스도 비슷하다.
스테이지에 특정 타워를 필수 요소로 설계했다면, 해당 타워를 '강제 배치'하게 설정했어야 맞지 않았을까 생각해 본다.
분명 스테이지 레벨 디자인을 하면서, 특정 타워가 들어가면 쉬울 것이라 생각하고 디자인을 했을 것이기에...

어쩌면 필자가 사회에 찌들어서 '알아가는 재미'와 '발견하는 재미'를 잃었을지도 모르겠다.
분명 어릴 적에는 '알아가는 재미'와 '발견하는 재미'가 있었는데.. 무언가 쫓기듯 인생을 살고 있기 때문일까?
나름 찾으려고 노력하고 많은 시간 할애하면서 플레이 했지만, 여전히 어려운 곳은 어려웠고, 말이 안되는 스테이지는 여전히 말이 안되었다.
필자가 생각하는 것을 반증할 수 있는 요소가 바로 '스팀 업적'인데 스테이지 30개를 클리어한 유저가 전체 구매자의 4.6%인 것을 감안하면, 진짜 난이도가 어려운 것은 맞다.


▷그 외
이 정도면 개발자는 100% 변태가 맞다.
또는, 2015년도 작품이기 때문에, 지금은 더욱 나은 횡보를 보여줄 수 있다.
하지만, 필자는 1에서 너무 데었기 때문에 2,3은 굳이 플레이할 것 같진 않다.
나름 하루에 1~2시간 투자해서 특정 스테이지 별 3개를 달성하려고 많은 시간을 할애했지만....
역시는 역시.

==============================================

Dungeon Warfare is a meticulously designed tower defense experience developed and published by Valsar that distinguishes itself by shifting the genre’s focus away from traditional towers and into the deliberate, often brutal use of traps. Rather than defending a base with static turrets or magical spells, the game casts the player as a dungeon architect whose sole purpose is to construct elaborate death corridors to stop waves of overconfident adventurers from reaching their goal. This inversion of perspective immediately gives Dungeon Warfare a strong identity, framing every level as a tactical puzzle where planning, placement, and timing matter far more than raw numbers.

The core gameplay revolves around building and refining trap layouts within tightly designed dungeon maps. Each stage provides a fixed layout with chokepoints, corridors, pits, and elevation changes that naturally influence how enemies move. Your task is to exploit these features by placing traps that interact with both the environment and each other. Spikes, flamethrowers, spring traps, harpoons, crushers, and rolling hazards can be combined into deadly chains, where one trigger feeds seamlessly into the next. The satisfaction comes not from overwhelming enemies with sheer firepower, but from watching carefully planned synergies funnel, stall, and ultimately obliterate entire waves with ruthless efficiency.

Enemy design plays a crucial role in keeping the experience engaging. Dungeon Warfare introduces a wide variety of adventurers, each with distinct behaviors, resistances, and vulnerabilities. Light enemies can be tossed into pits or flung across rooms, while heavily armored foes require layered damage and precise timing to bring down. Mixed waves force players to abandon one-size-fits-all solutions and adapt their setups to account for speed differences, armor types, and special abilities. As the game progresses, success depends on anticipating how enemies will react to traps rather than simply reacting once they appear.

Progression is handled through a persistent upgrade system that rewards experimentation and replay. Completing levels and killing enemies earns experience that can be invested into global upgrades affecting your entire arsenal. These upgrades don’t just increase raw damage, but also enhance trap utility through effects like faster cooldowns, longer activation times, or improved control. This creates meaningful long-term growth while preserving the importance of clever placement. Even early traps remain relevant late into the game, provided they are used intelligently and supported by complementary mechanics.

A standout feature is the game’s difficulty and modifier system, which allows players to tailor the challenge to their skill level. Optional runes can be activated to make enemies tougher, faster, or more numerous in exchange for greater rewards. This system transforms familiar levels into fresh challenges, encouraging players to revisit earlier maps with new constraints and strategies. Endless-style modes further extend replayability, pushing players to test how long their designs can hold up against increasingly relentless waves.

Visually, Dungeon Warfare adopts a crisp pixel-art style that prioritizes clarity over spectacle. Every trap and enemy is clearly readable, which is essential in a game where split-second observation can determine success or failure. Animations are punchy and expressive, making each successful trap activation feel impactful. Sound design reinforces this feedback loop, with satisfying audio cues for impalements, launches, and crushing blows that enhance the visceral pleasure of watching a well-built defense perform flawlessly.

The pacing of the game strikes a strong balance between action and planning. While waves unfold quickly and can become chaotic, the pause-and-build structure allows players to step back, reassess their layouts, and make adjustments between rounds. This rhythm encourages thoughtful iteration rather than frantic micromanagement, rewarding players who learn from mistakes and refine their designs over time. Levels feel compact and purposeful, rarely overstaying their welcome while still offering enough complexity to invite multiple solutions.

Dungeon Warfare is not without its limitations. Players who prefer constant novelty or large-scale progression systems may find the core loop familiar after many hours, as the game emphasizes mastery over reinvention. However, this focus is also its strength, as it consistently rewards strategic thinking and experimentation rather than grinding. The game trusts the player to engage deeply with its systems, and those willing to do so will find an impressive amount of depth beneath its straightforward presentation.

Taken as a whole, Dungeon Warfare stands as one of the more thoughtfully crafted tower defense games available on Steam. Its emphasis on trap synergy, enemy behavior, and environmental control creates a satisfying blend of strategy and spectacle that feels both challenging and fair. For players who enjoy solving lethal puzzles, refining systems, and watching carefully planned designs execute with brutal precision, Dungeon Warfare delivers a rewarding and highly replayable experience that exemplifies the genre at its best.

[h2]恶人视角下关卡众多的非常规塔防[/h2]
你作为一个恶魔，将经历50场战役来重铸魔族荣光。与一般的塔防不同，本作的敌人并没有固定的行进路线，而是会从入口到终点走最短距离。作为平衡，玩家可以放置路障[spoiler]可以直接压死敌人好评[/spoiler]来改变敌人的行进路线，认真规划可以极大降低攻关难度。

[h2]20种各具特色的陷阱[/h2]
本作最大的特色是有20种包括地刺，喷火器，绞肉机在内的各种邪恶陷阱。其中最值得说到的便是以推板、钩索、弹板、黑洞为代表的推拉位移体系。你可以借助这些陷阱聚集敌人或是将敌人直接推入岩浆等秒杀地形。游戏中不仅有着惯性和合力这些精细的物理模拟，每一个敌人还都有了详细的重量和碰撞体积——他们会互相堵路，甚至把队友挤下悬崖。

This is definitely on the deeper end of tower defense, requiring players to utilize a slow progression of new traps, consumables (think spells with cooldowns), and buffs to beat ever complex maze-based tower defense maps.

Some of the maps can be very difficult upon initial playthrough, but coming back after unlocking new items and methods of powering up result in quicker, easier wins.  

But don't worry, the game has several other optional elements to make stages much, much harder, resulting in a feedback look of challenge for those looking for insane depth.

Not all traps are made the same; after 30+ hours of gameplay, there are a few standouts and few losers, but most will find a home on some stages.  The ability to freely reset all your resources and focus on a new strategy at any time means you'll never feel stuck because of some arbitrary limit beyond natural progression.

Overall, it's definitely on the strong end of the tower defense genre.  There are no right answer, just some better than others.
